summary:
Allwork.Space reports, citing Rediff, that India's coworking sector has drawn $945.5 million in private equity investment since 2016, driven by growing demand for managed flexible office space among large companies. Investment in the first half of 2026 reached $30.9 million, already exceeding the $24.3 million recorded across all of 2025. The peak year was 2022, with $594.5 million in inflows.

Flexible workspace operators accounted for 24% of the 48 million square feet of office space leased across eight major Indian cities in the first half of 2026. The operating model involves leasing space from property owners and repackaging it for businesses as managed offices and flexible workspace arrangements.

Demand is skewing enterprise. Enterprises made up 72% of seats in managed workspace centers, and global capability centers (GCCs) represented 52% of demand. The piece frames this as evidence that managed offices are now used by established companies, not just startups and small businesses, because flex space provides extra capacity and additional locations without committing to conventional long-term leases.

India's listed flex workspace players include WeWork India, Smartworks, Awfis and IndiQube. The Executive Center and Table Space have filed documents with India's securities regulator ahead of planned IPOs.

The article concludes that rising investment and enterprise demand suggest flexible workspace is becoming a larger structural component of how Indian companies plan and use office portfolios. The item is market and real estate investment coverage rather than workplace operations or workplace technology content; it does not address desk booking, visitor management, attendance tracking, hybrid policy mechanics or admin workload.
